# openlabs

> openlabs is an open source library of Docker-based security labs. Each lab is one vulnerable service, one brief, and one flag.

Read a page in full at its URL. Open a brief, run the service, find the flag. Verify with `python3 scripts/check.py labs/<track>/<lab>` from the repo root. Each lab documents one host port and runs offline after images are pulled. Flags look like `duck{...}`; this file carries no flags.

## Labs

- [Labs](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs): Every lab is one vulnerable service, one brief, one flag.
- [Aegis ctf](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/aegis-ctf): Chained API trust vulnerabilities across REST, GraphQL, and gRPC.
- [Cafe house rules](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/cafe-house-rules): A cafe rules site with a report bot and a guarded back-room route.
- [Cloudvault](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/cloudvault): A GraphQL document-ingestion API whose SSRF chain reaches a privileged internal vault.
- [Duck cross](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/duck-cross): A reports portal with a missing object-level authorization check.
- [Duck nest](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/duck-nest): An internal project workspace for staff and interns.
- [Duckexchange](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/duckexchange): A tenant document API with a gRPC transcoding authorization bypass.
- [Duckrpc archive](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/duckrpc-archive): A gRPC document archive with authentication and a SQL injection vulnerability.
- [Duckvault web ctf](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/duckvault-web-ctf): A document management API with a broken object-level authorization check.
- [Duckvault](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/duckvault): A records portal leaks an internal reference through broken access control and weak authorization.
- [Fieldops 360](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/fieldops-360): A tenant portal with email open tracking and an admin export surface.
- [Firmdrama](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/firmdrama): A law firm's meeting-room portal with chained API authorization flaws and a vulnerable legacy template rendere
- [Invoiceportal](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/invoiceportal): InvoicePortal is a SaaS platform for managing company invoices.
- [Nexawallet](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/nexawallet): An Android wallet app that mints its flag only after a player defeats two independent, in-process gates — a Fr
- [Nexora platform](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/nexora-platform): Nexora is a deliberately vulnerable B2B SaaS CTF that simulates a realistic Blind SSRF attack using GraphQL, O
- [Shopvault](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/shopvault): An e-commerce REST API whose authentication, lockout, and JWT signing weaknesses chain into manager-level acce
- [Snapconnect](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/snapconnect): SnapConnect is a small social app with profiles and avatars, served by a GraphQL API.
- [Snapsync](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/snapsync): A staff photo tool where a forged token and a hidden internal route reach the flag.
- [Switf01 hit3](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/switf01-hit3): A task-management platform with a chained REST, GraphQL, and gRPC attack path.
- [Techvault](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/techvault): An e-commerce GraphQL API with a chained authentication bypass, SSRF, and command injection vulnerability.
- [Threadline](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/threadline): A clothing store REST API. One customer sees more than they should.
- [Vault api](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/labs/vault-api): Inspect an internal employee management API and recover a protected employee archive. The lab starts with a lo

## Guides

- [Open source security labs](https://openlabs.duckurity.com): Run a real service. Find the flag. Verify the solve.
- [How to play](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/play): Clone, run, solve. Verify each flag from the repo root.
- [Tracks](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/tracks): Five lab families. Start with web.
- [Techniques](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique): Vulnerability classes, defined once and exercised across labs.
- [API version enumeration](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/api-version-enumeration): Learn how to map versioned API surfaces and spot legacy endpoints that no longer meet the current security pol
- [Authentication bypass](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/auth-bypass): The server trusts a client-supplied field instead of verifying identity against a real credential check.
- [Client-side authorization decisions](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/client-side-authorization-decisions): Learn why an authorization check implemented only in client code is not a security control, and how attacker c
- [Command injection](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/command-injection): User input reaches a shell command unsanitized, letting you run commands alongside the intended one.
- [Framework-level Frida hooking past ART inlining](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/frida-framework-level-hooking-past-art-inlining): Learn why a Java-layer Frida hook can silently miss, and how framework-level or native-layer hooking recovers 
- [Broken object-level authorization (IDOR)](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/idor): Learn how missing per-object checks expose records that an authenticated user should not be able to read or ch
- [Launching an Activity in-process with Frida](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/in-process-activity-launch-with-frida): A practical walkthrough of starting any Activity in a running Android app from an attached Frida session, with
- [Mass assignment](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/mass-assignment): Learn how automatic request binding can let a client change protected object properties.
- [A non-exported Activity is not an access boundary](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/non-exported-activity-is-not-an-access-boundary): Learn why android:exported="false" only blocks other apps, and why code running inside the same process can st
- [SQL injection](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/sqli): Learn how unsanitized query input can change database logic and expose records outside normal access rules.
- [Server-side request forgery (SSRF)](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/ssrf): The server fetches a URL you control, letting you reach internal services it can see but you normally can't.
- [Server-side template injection (SSTI)](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/technique/ssti): Learn why user input must be treated as template data, never as template source, and how to recognise unsafe r

## Rules

- [Contribute](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/contribute): Author a lab. One lab per pull request.
- [FAQ](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/faq): Accounts, source reading, offline runs. Short answers.
- [Rules](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/rules): Run offline. Keep one port. Guard the flags.

## Optional

- [Repository](https://github.com/Duckurity/openlabs): source, labs, and issue forms.
- [Sitemap](https://openlabs.duckurity.com/sitemap.xml): every page for discovery.
